cover_headline: India Approves Its First Dengue Vaccine, Qdenga, Ahead of 2027 Launch
facts: Qdenga is given in two doses three months apart and covers all four dengue serotypes
Nearly 34 percent of the global dengue burden is in India, the highest share of any country
DengiAll, India's indigenous single-dose candidate, is in Phase III trials with more than 13,000 volunteers

quote.text: All four dengue virus serotypes circulate in India, contributing to recurrent outbreaks
quote.speaker: Dr. Goh Choo Beng
quote.role: Takeda's head of medical affairs for its Southeast Asia and India cluster

end.headline: India Approves Its First Dengue Vaccine, Qdenga, Ahead of 2027 Launch
end.line: The DCGI has authorised Takeda's two-dose vaccine for ages 4 to 60, with no screening or prior infection needed.
